relations.predicate: turns the last cyclic coordinate into
relations.quote: The twist turns the last cyclic coordinate into the [Polynomial ring modulo $y^r+1$](poly-ring-y-r.md).
The twist rescales the coefficients of a [Convolution](convolution.md) so that its cyclic wrap on the last axis becomes a negative wrap in $R$.
It is applied after [Bluestein's chirp identity](bluestein-chirp.md) has turned the middle transform into a cyclic convolution.

symbols.name: last-axis exponent
symbols.meaning: An exponent on the last axis, with $0\le k<r$, indexing one coefficient.
symbols.quote: Let $k$ and $l$ be exponents on the last axis, with $0\le k,l<r$.

symbols.name: second last-axis exponent
symbols.meaning: A second exponent on the last axis, with $0\le l<r$, paired with $k$ in a product.
symbols.quote: Let $k$ and $l$ be exponents on the last axis, with $0\le k,l<r$.

symbols.name: cyclic variable
symbols.meaning: The variable of the cyclic ring $\mathbb C[z]/(z^r-1)$, whose exponents wrap modulo $r$.
symbols.quote: Let $z$ be the variable of the cyclic ring $\mathbb C[z]/(z^r-1)$, whose exponents wrap modulo $r$.

symbols.name: twist root
symbols.meaning: The root of unity $e^{\pi \mathrm i/r}$, whose $r$-th power is $-1$, used to rescale coefficients.
symbols.quote: Let $\zeta=e^{\pi \mathrm i/r}$, where $\mathrm i$ is the imaginary unit, so $\zeta^r=-1$.

symbols.name: cyclic product index
symbols.meaning: The exponent $j$, with $0\le j<r$, of the cyclic product $z^j$.
symbols.quote: Every sum $k+l$ can be written $k+l=j+hr$ with $0\le j<r$ and $h\in\{0,1\}$, where $j$ is the cyclic index of the product and $h$ records whether the exponent wrapped.

symbols.name: wrap flag
symbols.meaning: The flag $h\in\{0,1\}$ recording whether the exponent $k+l$ wrapped past $r$.
symbols.quote: Every sum $k+l$ can be written $k+l=j+hr$ with $0\le j<r$ and $h\in\{0,1\}$, where $j$ is the cyclic index of the product and $h$ records whether the exponent wrapped.

symbols.name: first entry coefficient
symbols.meaning: The untwisted coefficient $\alpha_k$ of the first entry at index $k$.
symbols.quote: Write $\alpha_k$ and $\beta_l$ for the untwisted coefficients of two entries, so the entries are $\sum_k \alpha_k\zeta^k y^k$ and $\sum_l \beta_l\zeta^l y^l$.

symbols.name: second entry coefficient
symbols.meaning: The untwisted coefficient $\beta_l$ of the second entry at index $l$.
symbols.quote: Write $\alpha_k$ and $\beta_l$ for the untwisted coefficients of two entries, so the entries are $\sum_k \alpha_k\zeta^k y^k$ and $\sum_l \beta_l\zeta^l y^l$.

symbols.name: remaining-axis index
symbols.meaning: An index tuple with one coordinate per remaining cyclic axis, each wrapping modulo its length.
symbols.quote: For the other axes, let $v$ be an index tuple with one coordinate per remaining cyclic axis, each wrapping modulo its length.

symbols.name: entry ring
symbols.meaning: The ring $\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)$ in which each entry on the remaining axes lives.
symbols.quote: Let $R=\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)$, so each entry on those axes is an element of $R$.
